# Best portable power stations for camping

The best pick depends on how much you need to run. Most weekend campers do well with a small unit of about 250-500Wh.

## Weekend tent or car camping (phones, lights, camera, CPAP)
- **Jackery Explorer 300 Plus** is PowerStationGearLab's top pick. It has 288Wh of LiFePO4, weighs about 8.3 lb, and costs about $249. Jackery's own site has replaced it with the Explorer 300 v2, so you'd buy the Plus through Amazon or other retailers. ([source](https://powerstationgearlab.com/best/best-portable-power-station-for-camping/))
- **EcoFlow River 3 Plus** has 286Wh and a 600W inverter, double the Jackery's, for about $269-299. It's expandable to 572Wh. ([source](https://powerstationgearlab.com/best/best-portable-power-station-for-camping/))
- **Bluetti EB3A** is the budget option at 268Wh and 600W, often under $180. ([source](https://powerstationgearlab.com/best/best-portable-power-station-for-camping/))
- **Bluetti Elite 30 V2** has 288Wh and 600W. TechRadar picked it as best on a budget. ([source](https://www.techradar.com/best/portable-power-stations))

I'd be cautious about the Anker SOLIX C300. One guide praises it at about $199, but OutdoorGearLab's lab testing scored it only 50 out of 100. ([OutdoorGearLab](https://www.outdoorgearlab.com/topics/camping-and-hiking/best-power-station))

## Bigger trips (electric cooler, string lights, longer stays)
- **Jackery Explorer 2000 v2** is OutdoorGearLab's best for off-grid camping. It scored 81, weighs 39 lb, and has 2,200W output and fast solar charging. It lacks battery expansion, and it was listed under $900 on Amazon. ([source](https://www.outdoorgearlab.com/topics/camping-and-hiking/best-power-station))
- **Jackery Explorer 1500 Ultra** is WIRED's best for camping. It has 1,536Wh, an IP65 rating, and a 5-year warranty. It was listed at $1,079 on Amazon. ([source](https://www.wired.com/gallery/best-portable-power-stations/))
- **Jackery Explorer 1000 v2** is TechRadar's best for camping. It's the mid-size step up at about 1,070Wh. ([source](https://www.techradar.com/best/portable-power-stations))
- **Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2** is the best value, per OutdoorGearLab. It was under $530 on sale and weighs 25 lb, but the fan is noisy. ([source](https://www.outdoorgearlab.com/topics/camping-and-hiking/best-power-station))

## Mid-size option with a direct buy link
**[BLUETTI AC180](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-ac180)** has 1,152Wh and an 1,800W inverter, and weighs about 35 lb. It's $499 at BLUETTI's US store, or $474.05 with code AFF5OFF according to Dealectric. It comes with a 5-year warranty and a 30-day return window. It has no expansion port. This is an affiliate link, and prices change, so check the final price at checkout. ([details](https://dealectric.com/bluetti-ac180))

## How to choose
- **Weight matters most for camping.** A 288Wh unit covers phones, lights, and a few CPAP nights. Turning off the CPAP humidifier helps a lot.
- **Add up your watts and hours.** A fridge at about 150W for 10 hours is roughly 1,500Wh, so you'd need the 1,500-2,000Wh class.
- **Look for LiFePO4 batteries.** They last longer in hot, cold, and dusty conditions.
- **Consider a solar panel** if you'll be out more than a couple of nights. Jackery's SolarSaga is well regarded. Non-Jackery panels on the 2000 v2 need an adapter cable, about $25.
- **Don't fly with these.** They exceed the 100Wh airline limit.

For most campers, I'd start with the Jackery 300 Plus or EcoFlow River 3 Plus. The Jackery is lighter and simpler, and the EcoFlow runs more demanding gear. Each guide above has "check price" links to Amazon and other retailers. I couldn't verify live prices, so confirm them before buying.

If you tell me your gear, trip length, and budget, I can narrow this to one pick.
